Show me Mars with 30% oxygen and low air.answer: No data at 0.38 g: all the experiments in the table are in microgravity. Among those with oxygen values, the closest to this scenario are PSI-69 (FLEX, 12-30% O2) and PSI-25 (BASS-II, 14-21%); I'm highlighting them.

Show me the Moon with 26.5% oxygen.answer: No data at 0.16 g: the table has no measurements at lunar gravity. The closest record is PSI-69 (FLEX), which tested oxygen between 12 and 30% in microgravity, a range that includes 26.5%.

What do we know about combustion at luna.answer: No data: in the table no experiment declares a gravity between 0 and 1 g. This is a gap: the records cover only microgravity.

Which experiments have oxygen data?.answer: Eight: PSI-69 (FLEX) between 12 and 30% O2, PSI-68 (FLEX-2) between 17 and 30%, PSI-25 (BASS-II) between 14 and 22.2%, PSI-159 between 38 and 39.4%, PSI-98 (Saffire-I) between 21.5 and 21.7%, PSI-99 (Saffire-II) between 21.5 and 22.1%, PSI-10 between 20.4 and 20.7% and PSI-39 (CFI) 21%. For the others the value is not available in the sources consulted.

Which experiments have a known airflow?.answer: PSI-25 (BASS-II) up to 40 cm/s, PSI-98 and PSI-99 (Saffire) 20 cm/s, PSI-100 (Saffire-III) 30 cm/s, PSI-106 (SLICE) from 18 to 71 cm/s, PSI-107 (SPICE) from 36.39 to 57.08 cm/s, PSI-102 (SAME) from 5 to 10 cm/s, PSI-101 (SAME-R) 8.1 cm/s and PSI-68 (FLEX-2) from 0.1 to 5 cm/s. For the others there is no declared value.

What is the flame temperature at 0.16 g?.answer: No data: the table contains neither flame temperatures nor measurements at 0.16 g.

What did Saffire-I study?.answer: PSI-98 (Spacecraft Fire Experiment-I) studied how quickly a large fire grows in low gravity and the flammability limits, with an airflow of 20 cm/s and oxygen between 21.5 and 21.7%.

Which pressures were tested?.answer: PSI-69 (FLEX) between 10.3 and 14.7 psia, PSI-68 (FLEX-2) between 7.35 and 14.7 psia (0.5-1.0 atm), PSI-99 (Saffire-II) 14.5 psia, PSI-159 about 13.7 psia, PSI-39 (CFI) 14.7 psia and PSI-10 between 14.87 and 14.96 psia. For the other experiments, no data.
